title: New to gamedev. What advice could you give that could make my life and game easier?
author: Wooden-Coconut6852

comments.author: Dignified_Cyclops
comments.body: Marketing starts before you start making the game.

replies.author: Wooden-Coconut6852
replies.body: How do I market something that doesn't exist

replies.author: SeasonedAdManager
replies.body: Is there a market that wants your game? If its a solo passion project and you don’t care about money or fame, then it doesn’t matter. If you want a player base, it doesn’t matter.

replies.author: That1guy4226
replies.body: That more or less means research the target market to see if the idea of the game would bring any demand I think, but idk

replies.author: Dignified_Cyclops
replies.body:
You need to start thinking of a game as a product, not everyone wants it or needs it, but some people might, you need to figure out who they are. You do this by doing  doing market research to see if it's viable. Do other games like it exist, what value does yours add to the genre. Who plays games like this, where can you reach those people?  
  
Knowing simple things like this will help you   
1) make a better game  
2) get it in front of the right people

You can of course waste your time and do it after you start building. But I assure you, it will make your life easier and your game better if you do it from day one.

comments.author: zunashi
comments.body: Whatsup. If you’re asking this question, you’re very new to the game. I suggest you watch a lot of developer vlogs on YouTube. They share tips and wisdom.

comments.author: je386
comments.body:
At least these three should be thought and implemented from the beginning:

i18n (Internationalization)  
l10n (Localization)  
a11y (Accessibility)

And, if possible, you also can choose a language or framework that supports multiplatform, so you have the option to release for more than one platform.

comments.author: thebuddybud
comments.body:
Dont be afraid to make mistakes.  
You learn sooo much by making and fixing mistakes

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body: Don't use ai for anything besides code. Iterating to get useful spirits or 3d assets takes forever

replies.author: Wooden-Coconut6852
replies.body: What's a good way to get 3d assets could you recommend?

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
Blender mcp or python code for blender. 
Both work ok. Humanoids are impossible. Robots and low poly works fine. Rigging and animation work well. 
But you will need iteration after iteration. Even for a very basic asset like a chest or a wall will need lots of Iterations. 

Always have visual references, create concept art with different perspectives of the same asset as reference for the ai. Set a goal and keep iterating and then be underwhelmed after 5 hours. 
Fable does the best job modeling. Astra does the best job texturing since anthropic doesn't have image gen.

replies.author: Far-Bank3492
replies.body: why would they iterate if they can just use tripo or meshy for generating 3d assets? they do everything now, smart uv unwrap and rigging as well

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
Because for most usecases they don't produce a game ready Asset. Humanoids work ok but when animating you can get problems. Sure it works but it's not perfect, as is blender mcp. 
I tried all of them and stuck with blender.
